items.review_rationale: Examined the defining restriction of a groupoid-fibred category: every fibre E_U is a setoid. This is a fibrewise restriction over C, not the assertion that the total category E is a setoid.

references.context: Category theory: category of objects of E over U with morphisms projecting to identity on U

references.disposition: The stated condition holds for every U in C; it is not equivalent to the total category being a setoid.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed both equivalent descriptions: a groupoid with trivial automorphism groups, and at most one arrow between any ordered object pair. Distinguish existence as an equivalence relation from a poset's antisymmetry.

references.context: Category theory: invertible endomorphisms of a given object in a groupoid

references.phrase: equivalence relation on objects by existence of an arrow
references.context: Set theory: equivalence relation determined by isomorphism of groupoid objects

references.phrase: at most one arrow between objects
references.disposition: For a groupoid with trivial automorphisms, this follows by cancellation of invertible arrows; no skeletal assumption is present.

items.review_rationale: Read the object, 1-morphism, and 2-morphism clauses of the fibred-setoid 2-category, ensuring that natural transformations lie over identity arrows of the base and functors commute with projections.

references.phrase: categories fibred in setoids over C
natural transformations over identity arrows of C
references.context: Category theory: natural transformations between functors over a base whose components project to identities

references.disposition: The restriction is essential: arbitrary natural transformations between the underlying functors are not the same 2-morphisms.

items.review_rationale: Read both independent variable-linearity clauses, including the role of fixed elements in the other input and the shared R-module structure. For noncommutative rings, sidedness would need separate conventions not supplied by this formulation.

references.context: Module theory: linear homomorphism in one argument of a two-variable mapping holding the other argument fixed

references.disposition: Both separate linearity requirements are imposed, rather than a single linearity condition on M×N.

items.review_rationale: Examined the universal property including the initial bilinear map, existence and uniqueness of its R-linear factorization for every target R-module P. The side-of-action convention is not silently inferred for noncommutative R.

references.context: Category and module theory: unique R-linear factor through the tensor universal bilinear map

references.disposition: Uniqueness and the quantification over all codomain modules are the substantive universal property, not an assumed chosen basis.

items.review_rationale: Read the biconditional only in the stated countably generated R-module context; flatness plus the tensor-comparison Mittag-Leffler condition characterizes projectivity here, not projectivity of all flat modules.

references.context: Module theory: generation of a module by a finite or countably infinite set of elements

references.disposition: Countable generation is a mandatory hypothesis of this particular characterization.

items.review_rationale: Inspected the natural tensor-product comparison into a product of tensors, with injectivity required for every indexed family of R-modules. No surjectivity, countable index restriction, or flatness is asserted in this definition.

references.context: Module theory: product module indexed by arbitrary family, with coordinatewise operations
Module theory: natural tensor-product-to-product comparison induced by projections

references.disposition: Every indexed family is permitted; the map need not be surjective and the index set need not be countable.

items.review_rationale: Read the uniform finite bound across all R-modules, with global dimension defined as the least such nonnegative integer. This does not assert that every module is projective or that the ring has finite cardinality.

references.phrase: there exists a finite integer n
references.disposition: Uniform finite upper bound across all R-modules, not a separate n that can vary with M.
Least integer upper bound is the actual global dimension, without assuming it is 0.
